description.narrative:
The Ministry of Social Solidarity has taken a leading role in providing access to employability services in Egypt to the most vulnerable people. With World Bank and public funding and funding from Norway through the ILO, it has expanded its social assistance programmes Takaful and Karama to 5 million households through a conditional cash transfer programme and has committed to extending "economic empowerment" services to recipients of social grants as part of the “Forsa” (empowerment) programme.
Through the Forsa programme, the Ministry of Social Solidarity introduced the following new employment services to the vulnerable people beneficiaries of the Takaful and Karama programmes:
Job fairs and training for employment schemes: including labour market needs assessments in the targeted Governorates, skills assessment of the target groups, matchmaking, monitoring and follow-up to increase the employability of Takaful and Karama beneficiaries and therefore their access to formal and wages employment Results: 4 Job Fairs organized through the project support, the ministry has a plan to implement 8 more in the coming period. 1000 job seekers employed through training for employment schemes by the project. The target implemented by the ministry by 2023 is 15,000 Job seekers.
Provision of entrepreneurship and financial education training through the implementing arms of the Ministry of Social Solidarity ( Partners NGOs). The training aims to support vulnerable women , beneficiaries of asset transfers, starting and sustaining new income generating activities. Results: A network of 38 trainers on Get a head and Financial Education has been deployed within the partner NGOs in the two targeted areas. 2000 women were trained on “Get a head and Financial education” through the EYE:FORSA project. The Ministry target in the two governorates is almost 6000 families. With funding from Norway, the ILO supported the Ministry of Social Solidarity in delivering services on entrepreneurial, vocational and employability training for poor households in 2 of the 8 selected Governorates, where the first wave of the Forsa programme has been implemented.
ILO reinforced the capacities of 54 civil society organizations (CSOs) responsible to manage, facilitate and coordinate the implementation of Forsa Programme interventions, under the self and wage employment components.
ILO trained and qualified 105 trainers in Asyut and Sharkia governorates on business management and employability skills training programs to support NGOs capacities in the implementation of the Forsa programme.
ILO promoted access to wage employment through the implementation of 31 workshops as part of the "Job Search Clubs" programme (employability skills training) in Asyut and 12 workshops in Sharkiya, with the participation of 804 (764 females and 40 males) job seekers. (numbers as of end July 23).
48 training courses were organized with the support of ILO on the combined version of ILO’s “GET Ahead” for basic entrepreneurial skills and "Financial Education" programs. These sessions were attended by 1125 beneficiaries of "Forsa" program in Asyut and Sharkiya with the objective to promote female self-employment. The training was intended to help women beneficiaries managing their microbusinesses with the assets transferred to them by the "Forsa" program.
